children: The U.S. trade deficit widened in July, according to data published by the Commerce Department Thursday.
U.S. imports were higher than exports by $88.6 billion, versus $71.2 billion in June. Analysts polled by The Wall Street Journal were expecting a $90 billion deficit.
The gap is the result of imports increasing 2.8% in July from the previous month, to $399.3 billion, while exports decreased 2.1% to $310.7 billion.
Imports of goods increased $11.4 billion in July, while exports of goods decreased $6.2 billion. Exports of crude oil decreased $4.5 billion.

International commerce has been affected by volatile tariffs that put the U.S. at odds with traditional trade partners. More recently, negotiations with Canada have failed to yield a deal, opening the door for steep levies from both sides. Wars in the Middle East, Russia and Ukraine are also disrupting energy and food trade.
